children: Dario Amodei took Wall Street to Claude nine, if only briefly. Shares in Anthropic

, the AI lab he runs, surged 34% on its debut Thursday, briefly valuing it at $2 trillion. But growth is slowing and profit is still uncertain. It puts the rest of the artificial intelligence trade under a cloud.
Anthropic's entrance onto public markets comes against an unsettled backdrop. The CBOE Volatility Index

, Wall Street's preferred fear gauge, has hovered above 25 this week - a level that typically deters bankers from pushing new listings. Shares in chipmakers, Big Tech groups and data-center operators known as neoclouds have swooned following midterm elections that elevated a crop of AI skeptics. The dramatic departure of Nvidia's
founder Jensen Huang adds more ambiguity.

Anthropic is the first large machine-learning model maker to go public. At its opening price, the enterprise is valued at 14.5 times next fiscal year's revenue forecasts from Needham and Morningstar. That is even richer than Elon Musk's SpaceX
, which trades at 9 times sales for the same period, according to Visible Alpha.

The problem is that IPO buyers are paying this premium just as Anthropic's breakneck growth faces signs of deceleration. Revenue surged more than 1,200% in the first nine months of this year from a year earlier. But spending on tokens passed through the company's models rose just 3% in the week of November 15 relative to a month ago among businesses tracked by Ramp AI.

There are other reasons to doubt the durability of its economics. The falling price customers are paying per token is a sign of Anthropic's slipping pricing power. Its operating margin slipped to -3% in the third quarter from 8% in the second quarter, partly reflecting the soaring expense of energy. And Anthropic has committed some $900 billion to the chips, cloud services and data centers needed to train and run its AI models, with more than $70 billion due over the 12 months following September 2026.
Public investors will now have the opportunity to scrutinize those trade-offs every three months. The reaction in adjacent sectors suggests the market is already uneasy. Nvidia and Broadcom
shares fell 1.6% on Thursday, while neocloud names CoreWeave
and Nebius dropped 3.1% and 6%, respectively. Anthropic's own stock later traded below its $111.50 debut price.

Ultimately, Anthropic's ability to turn the proceeds it raised into profitable revenue depends partly on a less glamorous issue: whether data centers and chips can actually arrive on time. A stellar market debut may buy the AI industry another day of confidence, and perhaps help keep the server farm boom alive for a while. But the foundations look fragile.
Follow Karen Kwok on LinkedIn and X.
Anthropic's stock began trading on November 19, opening at $111.50 per share, 34% above the $83 initial public offering price.
The Claude chatbot maker and certain selling stockholders sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece in an upsized IPO, above the marketed range of $70 and $78 each.
Shares of Anthropic traded at $97 a share at 1217 ET.
